result.title: Wireless AI Networks: Co-Adapting Communication Resources and Distributed Intelligence
result.summary: Distributed artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly relies on wireless networks, where communication and computing resources shape how AI tasks are configured and executed. However, resource availability alone does not determine how effectively these tasks can be supported, since different information selections and transmission strategies may yield different AI performance under the same resource constraints. To address this challenge, this article presents Wireless AI Networks as a unified design perspective for bidirectional adaptation between wireless communication and distributed intelligence. Specifically, an AI-executable resource budget characterizes candidate AI configurations, while task-level information value guides their selection and wireless resource allocation. Building on these principles, a wireless-AI co-adaptation framework coordinates resource abstraction, joint configuration and allocation, and execution feedback. Two complementary experiments illustrate this perspective: update selection and statistical correction improve federated learning under identical model-update payload budgets, while sensitivity-aware power allocation reduces model accuracy degradation under the same average transmit-power constraint. Together, these results highlight the importance of coordinating resource feasibility and task-level information value in distributed AI execution.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「Wireless AI Networks」视角，用任务级信息价值指导通信资源分配与分布式 AI 配置，并通过联邦学习更新筛选和敏感度感知功率分配两个实验说明其作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在固定预算下按任务级信息价值筛选信息」的表述可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、latent 内容保留与预算-收益权衡可供核查，但场景为无线分布式学习，无 latent 推理状态。
